{{Short description|Cellular automaton with probabilistic rules}}
{{technical|date=June 2013}}
A '''stochastic cellular automaton''' ('''SCA'''), also known as a '''probabilistic cellular automaton''' ('''PCA'''), is a type of [[computational model]]. It consists of a grid of cells, where each cell has a particular state (e.g., "on" or "off"). The states of all cells evolve in discrete time steps according to a set of rules.

Unlike a standard [[cellular automaton]] where the rules are deterministic (fixed), the rules in a stochastic cellular automaton are [[Stochastic|probabilistic]]. This means a cell's next state is determined by chance, according to a set of probabilities that depend on the states of neighboring cells.<ref name="vichniac2">{{citation |last=Vichniac |first=G. |title=Simulating physics with cellular automata |journal=Physica D |volume=10 |issue=1–2 |pages=96–115 |year=1984 |bibcode=1984PhyD...10...96V |doi=10.1016/0167-2789(84)90253-7}}.</ref>

Despite the simple, local, and random nature of the rules, these models can produce complex global patterns through processes like [[emergence]] and [[self-organization]]. They are used to model a wide variety of real-world phenomena where randomness is a factor, such as the spread of [[Wildfire|forest fires]], the dynamics of disease epidemics, or the simulation of [[ferromagnetism]] in physics (see [[Ising model]]).

As a mathematical object, a stochastic cellular automaton is a discrete-time [[random dynamical system]]. It is often analyzed within the frameworks of [[Interacting particle system|interacting particle systems]] and [[Markov chain|Markov chains]], where it may be called a system of '''locally interacting Markov chains'''.<ref>{{citation |last=Toom |first=A. L. |title=Locally Interacting Systems and their Application in Biology: Proceedings of the School-Seminar on Markov Interaction Processes in Biology, held in Pushchino, March 1976 |volume=653 |year=1978 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |publisher=Springer-Verlag, Berlin-New York |isbn=978-3-540-08450-1 |mr=0479791}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author1=R. L. Dobrushin |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0Wa7AAAAIAAJ&q=locally+interacting+markov+chains+toom+Dobrushin&pg=PA181 |title=Stochastic Cellular Systems: Ergodicity, Memory, Morphogenesis |author2=V. I. Kri︠u︡kov |author3=A. L. == Formal definition ==

From the perspective of [[probability theory]], a stochastic cellular automaton is a discrete-time [[Markov process]]. The configuration of all cells at a given time is a state <math>\eta</math> in a [[product space]] <math>E=\prod_{k \in G} S_k</math>. Here, <math>G</math> is a graph representing the grid of cells (e.g., <math>\mathbb{Z}^d</math>), and each <math>S_k</math> is the finite set of possible states for the cell <math>k</math> (e.g., <math>S_k = \{0, 1\}</math>).

The transition probability, which defines the dynamics, has a product form:
:<math> P(d\sigma | \eta) = \bigotimes_{k \in G} p_k(d\sigma_k | \eta) </math>
where <math>\sigma</math> is the next configuration and <math>p_k(d\sigma_k | \eta)</math> is a probability distribution on <math>S_k</math>. 

Locality is a key requirement, meaning the probability of a cell <math>k</math> changing its state depends only on the states of its neighbors. This is expressed as <math>p_k(d\sigma_k | \eta) = p_k(d\sigma_k | \eta_{V_k})</math>, where <math>V_k</math> is a finite neighborhood of cell <math>k</math> and <math>\eta_{V_k}</math> are the states of the cells in that neighborhood. See <ref>[https://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/tel-00002203v1 P.-Y. Louis PhD]</ref> for a more detailed introduction from this point of view.

== Examples of stochastic cellular automaton ==

=== Majority cellular automaton ===

There is a version of the [[majority problem (cellular automaton)|majority cellular automaton]] with probabilistic updating rules. See the [[Toom's rule]].

=== Relation to lattice random fields ===
PCA may be used to simulate the [[Ising model]] of [[ferromagnetism]] in [[statistical mechanics]].<ref name="vichniac2" />
Some categories of models were studied from a statistical mechanics point of view.

=== Cellular Potts model ===
There is a strong connection<ref name="CPM">{{cite book|title=Probabilistic Cellular Automata
    | first1=Sonja E. M. | last1 =Boas
    | first2=Yi| last2=Jiang
    | first3=Roeland M. H. |last3=Merks
    |first4=Sotiris A. |last4=Prokopiou
     |first5=Elisabeth G. |last5=Rens
|doi =10.1007/978-3-319-65558-1_18
| editor-last1=Louis |editor-first1=P.-Y.
| editor-last2=Nardi |editor-first2=F. R.
|publisher=Springer
 |date=2018
 |isbn=9783319655581
|chapter=Chapter 18: Cellular Potts Model: Applications to Vasculogenesis and Angiogenesis | hdl=1887/69811 }}</ref>
between probabilistic cellular automata and the [[cellular Potts model]] in particular when it is implemented in parallel.

=== Non Markovian generalization ===
The [[Galves–Löcherbach model]] is an example of a generalized PCA with a non Markovian aspect.
